newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Dollar/mark rise spurs BCE currency futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/mark rise spurs BCE currency futures trade.

text.p: Volume in currency futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) rose on Thursday as spot dollar/mark rates continued their rise, although trading was slack on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE).

The BCE saw 9.51 billion forints turnover, with two thirds shared by the mark and the Swiss franc. The BSE saw just one contract, an 89 million forint agency cross for March dollars, although prices rose for almost all dollar maturities.
"The dollar/mark cross was certainly the main factor in the today's large turnover of mark futures (on the BCE)," said Janos Fonodi of Termin-Broker.
Dealers said interest in mark futures reflected a feeling that the dollar will move even higher in the medium term.

On the BCE, the September mark saw 24,000 lots traded as the price fell 30 fillers to 112.2 forints. The March mark also fell, by 25 fillers to 104.05. The central bank (NBH) Thursday spot fix for the mark was 103.21.

The Swiss franc, which offers an attractive interest rate differential with the devaluing forint, saw 25,940 lots traded, mainly for September, which rose 80 fillers to 131.00, as against an NBH spot rate of 119.74 forints.
The dollar rose 60 fillers to 179.00 for March but its biggest rise was 74 fillers to 185.44 for June. The dollar ended Thursday spot trade at 178.97/178.02.

The forint floats in the NBH's intervention range against a currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar, and is devalued against the basket by 1.2 percent per month under the NBH's crawling peg devaluation policy.
On the BSE the dollar rose for all contracts except September, which was steady, by between 13 and 87 fillers.
Only the May mark moved on the BSE, falling 37 fillers to 107.63.
The BSE and BCE currency futures markets are currently not open to foreign investors.
